paper_metadata.title: Portfolio rebalancing experiments using the Quantum Alternating Operator Ansatz

summary: The paper evaluates QAOA and the Quantum Alternating Operator Ansatz for discrete portfolio rebalancing on an 8‑asset portfolio (16 qubits) using an idealized simulator. In a six‑month simulated rebalancing scenario with trading cost T=0.015, the hard‑constraint ansatz with p=4 produced portfolios within ~5% of the brute‑force optimal adjusted returns and achieved the optimal risk solution when λ=1. All experiments are conducted on a noiseless simulator and compared against brute‑force classical solutions.

experiments.description: Single-portfolio portfolio rebalancing solved with QAOA soft-constraint formulation on an idealized gate-model simulator, using daily-return data and p=1 parameter sweep.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Two-spin encoding per asset: each asset position z_i is represented by binary/spin variables (x_i^+, x_i^-) / (s_i^+, s_i^-), giving 2 qubits per asset; for N=8 assets this yields 16 binary variables/qubits.
problem_formulation.objective_function: C_soft(s) = C_RR(s) + C_TC(s) + P_INV(s), where C_RR is the Markowitz risk-return term, C_TC is the trading-cost term, and P_INV = A(\sum_i z_i - D)^2 enforces the investment constraint.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Soft constraint via quadratic penalty term P_INV; unconstrained QAOA mixer B = sum_i sigma_x_i.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Ising/QAOA cost operator obtained by substituting Pauli-Z operators for spins in C_soft(s).

problem_instance.description: Discrete portfolio rebalancing for an 8-stock ASX.20 portfolio with target holding D=4 lots.

dataset_specification.preprocessing: daily average returns and covariance matrix computed from 2017 daily returns; initial experiment uses daily returns, then annualized returns by multiplying averages and covariances by 250

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Daily returns used first; then annualized returns obtained by multiplying both mean returns and covariance matrix by 250 to improve scaling.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Single p=1 circuit sweep over beta and gamma; results shown as expectation landscape.

implementation_details.classical_solver: Nelder-Mead optimizer mentioned for QAOA outer loop in later experiments; not explicitly tied to this single-circuit sweep
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Brute-force calculation of penalty scaling A using max-min of unconstrained cost; data scaling from daily to annualized returns.

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: periodic landscape in beta-gamma; slow variation with poor scaling, improved after annualization

speedup_claims.caveats: No asymptotic or empirical speedup claim is made; this is a simulator study focused on scaling and expectation landscapes.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(p) circuit depth for QAOA; problem size 2^16 state space for N=8 assets with two-spin encoding
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: brute force over 2^16 states for this instance

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not discussed; experiment only evaluates parameter landscape for a 16‑qubit toy instance.
limiting_factors: Executed only on an idealized simulator
Very small problem size (8 assets / 16 qubits)
No comparison with scalable classical optimizers

experiments.description: Multi-period monthly portfolio rebalancing over six months using QAOA soft-constraint and hard-constraint formulations on a simulator, with trading costs and p=2/4.

algorithm.variant: QAOA soft-constraint vs Quantum Alternating Operator Ansatz hard-constraint

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Two-spin encoding per asset; 16 qubits total for 8 assets.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Monthly optimization of C_RR + C_TC (hard) or C_RR + C_TC + P_INV (soft), with adjusted returns and risk evaluated over 6 months.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Soft penalty vs hard parity-mixer constraint; optimization performed independently at each time step.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Ising cost operator from the monthly objective.

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compare total number of trades, adjusted returns, and average risk over 6 months against brute force optimum; results shown for lambda values 0.0, 0.9, and 1.0; p=2 and p=4.

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute number of trades, adjusted returns, and average risk over 6 months.

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports qualitative near-optimal performance and one case within 5% of the brute-force adjusted return for p=4, but does not claim computational speedup.

experiments.description: Multi-period portfolio rebalancing experiment over six months comparing QAOA soft-constraint formulation and Quantum Alternating Operator Ansatz hard-constraint formulation with trading costs, evaluated against brute-force optimal solutions.

algorithm.variant: standard QAOA (soft constraint) vs Quantum Alternating Operator Ansatz (hard constraint with parity mixers)

key_results: Portfolio rebalanced monthly for 6 months using annualized monthly return estimates.
Hard-constraint QAOA (alternating operator ansatz) achieved adjusted returns within ~5% of brute-force optimal when p=4.
For λ=1 (risk minimization), the hard-constraint formulation found the optimal risk solution for each of the 6 months at p=4.
Experiments used an 8‑asset portfolio (16 qubits via two-spin encoding) with target holding D=4.
